record.title: Singapore publishes quantum-safe migration milestones and pilot grant
record.summary: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency published quantum-safe migration milestones and launched a pilot grant on 14 October. Non-CII organizations exposed to quantum risks are advised to prepare a migration plan by the end of 2027 and aim to complete migration by 2035. CII owners have a 31 March 2027 plan-submission deadline, a 31 December 2031 migration target, and quantum-safe procurement considerations from 2028. The Quantum-Safe Kickstarter Grant is open to Singapore-incorporated non-government organizations for Singapore-based work, prioritizes CII owners, and covers up to 70% of eligible costs with 30% cash co-funding; funded pilots may last up to six months during the 1 November 2026–31 October 2027 grant period. No award, completed pilot or migration outcome is established.
organizations: Ministry of Digital Development and Information, Singapore

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency published a quantum-safe migration advisory on 14 October 2026. It advises non-CII organizations exposed to quantum risks to establish a migration plan by the end of 2027 and aim to complete migration by 2035; the advisory is broad guidance, not evidence that organizations have acted.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The official guidance sets separate CII milestones: submit migration plans by 31 March 2027, complete migration of CII systems by 31 December 2031, and account for quantum-safe considerations in new CII system procurement from 2028.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: CSA launched the Quantum-Safe Kickstarter Grant. Applications are open; the grant period runs from 1 November 2026 through 31 October 2027, with pilots lasting up to six months. It covers up to 70% of eligible project costs and requires a 30% cash contribution. Eligible applicants are non-government organizations registered and incorporated in Singapore undertaking work in Singapore; CII owners receive priority.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The published documents describe milestones, grant terms and required pilot reporting, but this review found no awards, completed pilots, organization-level migration progress or measured reduction in cryptographic risk.

evidence_gaps.description: The advisory sets milestones but no organization-level adoption, migration-plan submissions or CII procurement compliance data were found.

The grant is open, but no awards or completed pilot reports were available in the reviewed materials. The page says reports should document technical implementation, testing methods, results, limitations and resourcing.
No evidence yet shows that guidance or funded pilots reduce cryptographic exposure or improve migration readiness at ecosystem scale.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, extending migration guidance beyond critical infrastructure and funding early pilots could accelerate replacement of vulnerable cryptography in sensitive systems and surface practical transition barriers. The announcement establishes intent, not coverage, uptake or risk reduction.
limitations: The advisory recommends milestones; this review did not establish that the non-CII timelines are legally mandatory.
Grant terms establish funding rules and applicant eligibility, not award volume, recipient selection or successful migration.
No organization-level progress, completed pilots, measured performance, interoperability results or cryptographic risk reduction is reported.
Migration progress depends on cryptographic inventories, vendor readiness, legacy-system constraints and organizational implementation; these are not measured here.

brief.summary: Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency published quantum-safe migration milestones and launched a pilot grant on 14 October. Non-CII organizations exposed to quantum risks are advised to prepare a migration plan by the end of 2027 and aim to complete migration by 2035. technical.claimed_result: CSA’s published advisory recommends non-CII organizations exposed to quantum risks have migration plans by end-2027 and aim for completion by 2035; it sets CII milestones for 31 March 2027 plan submission, 31 December 2031 migration completion and quantum-safe procurement from 2028. The grant covers up to 70% of project costs with 30% cash co-funding, and funded pilots may last up to six months.
technical.demonstrated_result: CSA published the advisory and grant information pack on 14 October 2026. The documents specify differentiated milestones, Singapore applicant eligibility, grant coverage, timing and reporting requirements. No pilot award or migration outcome was reviewed.
technical.mechanism: CSA published risk-based migration milestones and practical advisory guidance; a time-bounded, co-funded grant supports operational pilots that test cryptographic discovery, system migration and legacy/OT transition, with participants required to report methods, findings and demonstrated impact.
technical.regime: Singapore organizations exposed to quantum-related cybersecurity risks. Non-CII organizations should plan by end-2027 and aim to complete migration by 2035; CII owners have separate plan and system migration milestones. The grant supports qualifying Singapore-incorporated non-government organizations conducting Singapore-based pilots, gives CII owners priority, covers up to 70% of eligible costs, and runs 1 November 2026–31 October 2027.
technical.reproducibility: The government guidance and grant terms are publicly inspectable. Future pilot reports are required to document technical implementation, testing methods, results, limitations and resourcing, but none was reviewed in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: CSA’s earlier June 2026 guidance for CII owners set a 2031 migration target. The 14 October advisory extends planning guidance to other organizations with a 2035 target and end-2027 plan milestone; the grant adds partial cash support for bounded migration pilots.

brief.title: Singapore publishes quantum-safe migration milestones and pilot grant
brief.why_it_matters: The guidance turns a broad quantum-readiness goal into dated planning, procurement and migration milestones, while the grant can help organizations test discovery and migration on real systems before a cryptographically relevant quantum threat exists. The rules create observable implementation checkpoints, but their effect depends on organizational uptake and pilot quality; no migration or risk-reduction result is yet established.
